clue.text: Fish taken to wharf

parts.note: had is a past participle meaning taken or held
a dock is a landing place where ships tie up

explanation.surface: A catch of fish is carried off to the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish related to the cod, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Listen to a number cheer

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Hearing a song can lift one's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' suggests a song, but it is just a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage them and raise their spirits, the verb sense of cheer.

clue.text: Thunderous notes introduce the ascending Muses

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so a group takes something inside

parts.note: D, E, A, F and G are all musical notes

indicators.note: in a down clue ascending means read upwards, back to front

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Loud chords herald the arrival of the goddesses of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes are four and one: the upturned Muses go between the F and the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderous noise is so loud it seems able to stop one hearing, which is the literal sense of the answer.

clue.text: It loves speed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero is O
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Something enjoys going fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun, but in old slang it is sex appeal, as in the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: It in 1920s slang meant sexual magnetism, and oomph is another informal word for the same attractiveness or vigour.

clue.text: Fell very low

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fell is to strike down to the ground
second meaning: as of prices, reduced to the minimum

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past tense of fall, but it is the verb to bring down a tree or person.
explanation.definitionFit: Knock down is the verb for striking someone to the floor, and knockdown prices are bargain ones, cut as far as possible.

clue.text: First form about to drop a clanger

definitions.note: the answer is used as a verb here, meaning to err

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to form something is to make it
first is written 1st, with the 1 read as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A first-former is on the point of committing an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First form' looks like a school class, but the two words are separate pieces. To drop a clanger is British slang for making an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: As an intransitive verb the word means to err or go wrong in judgement, which is what dropping a blunder amounts to.

clue.text: A subject many aspiring teachers hate, specially in the beginning

definitions.text: A subject many aspiring teachers hate, specially in the beginning

indicators.note: in the beginning points to the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Trainee teachers often dread one particular subject, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and also spells it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics is a school subject that many trainee teachers find daunting, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Vessel repaired in base depot

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, here in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship is being fixed at a naval base's depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a fast motorboat, and any boat is a vessel that floats and carries people.

clue.text: An airborne unit is frightening

parts.note: an is the article a
a wing is a unit of an air force

explanation.surface: A flying squadron makes a scary sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To awe people is to fill them with dread and wonder, so awing means inspiring fear.

clue.text: Builder, a Cockney fellow, ruined his lady, they say

indicators.note: they say means the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.words: a Cockney fellow, ruined his lady
parts.note: a Cockney drops his h's, so he and her lose their first letters, and ruined is wrecked

explanation.surface: A Londoner reports that a builder seduced and ruined his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose speech drops the h at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who sets up or constructs things such as buildings and scaffolding, so a builder.

clue.text: Frighten a novice with a gun

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate shown by a novice driver
a gun is a firearm, or arm

explanation.surface: Scaring a beginner by brandishing a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate, so L stands for a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to make them afraid or anxious, a direct synonym of frighten.

clue.text: Unreservedly offered at eye level

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put at stake openly, as when a job is laid down without holding anything back
second meaning: in a gallery, a picture hung at the height of the viewer's eye

explanation.surface: Goods put openly on sale and displayed at eye height on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the Royal Academy, where the best pictures were hung along a line at eye height.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means staked or risked without reservation, and also describes a painting hung at the most favourable viewing height.

clue.text: Ague necessitates admitting men to hospital

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word takes others inside it

parts.note: if a job takes time it necessitates it
hes is a plural of he, a man
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A fever requires men to be taken into hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The men and the hospital go in together, straight after the first letter of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is a malarial fever marked by fits of shivering, which is the informal shakes.

clue.text: Appreciate little Italian number

parts.note: dig is slang for appreciate or like
It. is the short form of Italian

explanation.surface: Enjoying a short Italian song or number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals an abbreviation, not a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any single figure from nought to nine, so it is a number.

clue.text: Denial we hear straight from the horse's mouth

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a denial

explanation.surface: A refusal heard first-hand, from the most reliable source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight from the horse's mouth' is an idiom for first-hand information, but here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinny is the sound a horse makes, so it literally comes out of the animal's mouth.

clue.text: Cases with holes in them can't stand close scrutiny

parts.words: Cases with holes in them can't
parts.note: surface reading: legal arguments full of flaws fail when examined
setter's reading: containers that leak cannot keep liquid in

explanation.surface: Weak legal arguments collapse under careful examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The cases are both legal arguments and vessels; the leaky kind cannot keep liquid in.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is said to bear examination when it is sound, the idiom for surviving close inspection.

clue.text: Turned red, perhaps, or blue

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
red is an example of a colour

explanation.surface: Someone blushed, or perhaps went pale with cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' and 'blue' look like a pair of colours, but blue is the definition, meaning risque.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are smutty or indecent, and off-colour also describes humour that is slightly improper.

clue.text: Shag, I feel, could be treated as a predatory bird

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a shag, a seabird, may be regarded as a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: A shag is a cormorant-like seabird, which makes 'Shag' look like the definition; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eagles are large raptors that catch fish, so they are hunting birds of prey.

clue.text: Immediately uncontrollable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at once, without consideration, as when an offer is rejected
second meaning: beyond control, as of an unruly crowd

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words seem to describe something going wild at once; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something out of hand is to do it straight away, and a situation out of hand has got beyond control.

clue.text: Where Gaelic was spoken. English had not started to spread

indicators.note: to spread is to scatter, so the letters are scattered into a new order
something not started lacks its beginning, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A region where Gaelic was spoken before English began to take over.
explanation.walkthrough: English loses its first letter before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Highlands are the mountainous north of Scotland, the traditional heartland of Scottish Gaelic speech.

clue.text: The most difficult Latin is set first

indicators.note: first tells us which piece is placed at the front

parts.note: a jelly that has set has gone hard
est is the Latin word for is

explanation.surface: Latin is placed first, as the toughest subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardest is the superlative of hard in the sense of difficult, so it means the most testing.

clue.text: Child takes me about — it symbolizes kinship

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child carries me around, a picture of family bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Among many peoples a totem is an animal or emblem that marks a clan, standing for the shared family connection.

clue.text: Within a very short distance, a sort of local fellow

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits in the other

parts.note: mm is the abbreviation for a millimetre, a tiny length

indicators.note: a sort of means a version of, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from just round the corner, a sort of local character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'very short distance' is not a letter A; it belongs to the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm is a man's name, and crosswords often define a first name loosely as a fellow.

clue.text: Frenchman with a point to make again

parts.note: Rene is a common French man's name
W is west, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with an argument he wants to press again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A point' looks like an argument, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore it or produce it afresh, so it is made new once more.

clue.text: in the main, it resembles saltpetre

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of main and the start of the next two words

explanation.surface: Seawater, on the whole, is rather like a salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea, which suits a clue about salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is the older name for potassium nitrate, the same mineral salt also called saltpetre.

clue.text: A little money advanced: if accepted, money becomes ample

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so the earlier pieces go inside

parts.note: the pul is a small coin of Afghanistan
a small sum advanced is a sum lent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small loan, if agreed, turns into plenty of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The pul is an obscure coin, a hundredth of an afghani; it wraps round the loan and the if.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, and plentiful likewise describes a supply that is abundant.

clue.text: Trojan gets the wind up in the afternoon

indicators.note: in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: pm marks times after noon

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, back to front

parts.note: air is a light wind or breeze

explanation.surface: A man of Troy takes fright in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the wind up' is an idiom for becoming scared, but here wind and up are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Homer's Iliad, so he was a Trojan.

clue.text: Become thin and light

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to narrow gradually towards one end
second meaning: a slender candle or wick used to light things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin and light' reads as a pair of adjectives describing weight loss, but light is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a long thin candle that gives light, and to taper is to grow gradually narrower.

clue.text: Hen bird losing its head — the heather is calling

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word in front is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
a tit is a small songbird
ling is the common heather

explanation.surface: A beheaded hen bird lies on the heather, which seems to be calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hen bird' looks like a female bird, but they are two pieces; only Hen loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone or something is to give it a name or title, which is what calling it means.

clue.text: Scotsman falls into the river quietly

indicators.note: falls into means drops inside, so one word ends up within another

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot tumbles silently into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian direction piano means soft, so a passage played piano is played quietly.

clue.text: Other people objectively accept roundabout proposition

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one word holds the next pieces

parts.note: them is the object form of they, used for other people
split as round, the ring-shaped letter O, and about, the Latin-derived re used in business letters

explanation.surface: Others agree to a circuitous suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' looks like one word meaning indirect, but it splits into round and about. 'Objectively' points to the grammatical object form.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a statement to be proved, which is the technical sense of a proposition.

clue.text: This could make me a lord

definitions.text: This could make me a lord

indicators.note: could make suggests something that may be formed from the following letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hopeful wonders what honour would raise them to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being granted the rank and title of an earl would make the holder a peer, that is, a lord.
